summary: H.R. 10498, titled the "Illegal War Refund Act," requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to calculate the total annual economic costs borne by U.S. taxpayers due to the Iran war, including increased interest rates, fuel prices, food prices, and inflation. The bill directs that funds be transferred from unobligated Department of Defense accounts to the Secretary of the Treasury to make equal annual payments to U.S. taxpayers and their dependents starting in fiscal year 2027.

affected_groups.effect: Receive annual payments funded by transferred Department of Defense moneys.
Subject to prorated transfers of unobligated funds from accounts excluding military personnel, military construction, and the Defense Health Program.

key_provisions: Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to calculate the total economic costs of the Iran war on U.S. taxpayers each fiscal year by October 15, starting in fiscal year 2027.
Includes costs from negative impacts such as increased interest rates, fuel prices, food prices, and inflation in the economic calculation.
Mandates the transfer of funds equal to the calculated amount from unobligated Department of Defense funds to the Secretary of the Treasury.
Excludes military personnel, military construction, and Defense Health Program accounts from the fund transfers.
Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to make equal payments to eligible U.S. taxpayers and their dependents by October 30 of each fiscal year starting in 2027.
Prohibits any letter, check, or payment document from bearing the name, signature, or likeness of any elected official.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact formula for calculating the total economic costs of the Iran war.
The precise dollar amount of payments individuals and dependents will receive.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10498, titled the "Illegal War Refund Act," requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to calculate the total annual economic costs borne by U.S. taxpayers due to the Iran war, including increased interest rates, fuel prices, food prices, and inflation. The bill directs that funds be transferred from unobligated Department of Defense accounts to the Secretary of the Treasury to make equal annual payments to U.S. taxpayers and their dependents starting in fiscal year 2027.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a regular mechanism to transfer federal defense funds to individual taxpayers and dependents to offset economic costs attributed to the Iran war, affecting the budget allocations of the Department of Defense and providing direct payments to tax-filing individuals.
